rationale: B wins because it keeps the story inside the facts and makes the proof burden the point: "A 22% drop in no-shows: what Mindbody's AI pilot proves and what it doesn't" is exactly the skeptical trade angle this update can support. A has flashier angles, but "Mindbody's AI treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" and "it's adding AI to both" turn supplied facts into invented product architecture. That is how a clever pitch becomes a correction request.
gaps_in_A: "Mindbody's AI treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" is not in the update. Mindbody powers 50,000 studios and salons, but nothing says the assistant pools all calendars into one aggregate dataset.
"it's adding AI to both" overclaims the ClassPass connection. The facts say Mindbody owns ClassPass; they do not say this studio-side assistant touches ClassPass.
"AI-native challengers out-innovate slow incumbents" invents a competitive frame before naming a single challenger or showing that startups promised this feature.
"PE-owned SaaS companies" goes beyond "privately held after a take-private deal." If ownership matters, identify the owner before building an angle on private-equity strategy.
gaps_in_B: "Next step: `journalist-fit-check`" is the wrong first move. Its own copy says the pilot methodology and a named studio are prerequisites; fact-checking should come before reporter matching.
"small-business columnist at a regional business outlet" only works with a named local studio and geography. Without that, regional business press has no local peg.

"The assistant uses booking data per studio" is safer than A's aggregate-data leap, but still an assumption. The update says booking data; it does not specify whether recommendations are studio-local, pooled, or hybrid.

It parks the ClassPass ownership fact almost entirely in "Does the assistant fill freed spots from the studio's own waitlist only, or does ClassPass inventory come into play?" A cautious platform-power angle could exist without claiming product integration.
